title: Coach Cockpit
goal: Open the tool and know within seconds which team needs the coach, and by when — then act from the card, not from a hunt.

zones.name: header
zones.purpose: The template's header: the screen's name, and the freshness beside the ONE control that refreshes it (PageHeader arrives through OverviewPageTemplate, not as a direct import) — never under the title, where it reads as a tagline and steals the eye. AutoStatus is a FACT (when transcripts were last looked for) and only re-runs that collection; Refresh re-reads everything and waits only for the workbook, because that is what it is pressed for. Every removed button here (board refresh, sync teams) was removed because a coach cannot know WHEN to press it — the windows top things up by themselves and this header says so instead of asking.

zones.name: notices
zones.purpose: Only what STOPS WORK, and nothing when the machine is healthy — the contract that makes a notice safe at the top of the busiest screen. SetupNeeded names the missing prerequisite in terms of the CLI the coach is actually on; PastMeetings is the ask-first scanner for a coach with months of history before the install: a button, because the scan walks the whole calendar and only the coach knows there is history worth finding.

zones.name: band
zones.purpose: What the programme asks NOW and by when — a band above the work, not a card competing with it. It earns its place by being about TIME, which changes every day it is looked at; everything that does not change with the date (the rubric, the winning criteria) stays out on purpose. It reads before the board because a coach who knows the deadline reads the ranking differently.

zones.name: board
zones.purpose: One card per team, ranked by risk band — Needs you now, Drifting, Steady — so reading order IS priority order. Each card states the verdict as a Badge, the reasons as sentences with the number said once inside the reason, the stage counted from sessions that actually happened, who owes what with the coach's own share marked, and the drafted reply ready to send. Evidence sits beside the verdict and never moves the score; a busy team scores no differently, and a test pins that. The card is the dashboard — the second overview screen this app once had was deleted for reading the same rows through a lens.

states.loading: Spinner beside the header's status while a background collection runs; the board itself renders from the local computation and does not blank.
states.empty: EmptyState explaining the name-matching rule when no team resolves to this coach — a first run, or a name the SoT spells differently — with the way to fix the name, because an empty board with no explanation reads as a broken tool.
states.error: Alert above the board naming which source failed (the board file, or the calendar) and keeping the last computed board on screen: a stale answer plus the reason beats a blank page.

acceptance: On a healthy machine the notices zone renders nothing at all.
Freshness reads beside the refresh control, never under the title.
The first card on the board is the team most at risk, and its band says so in words.
A number appears once per reason — never as a count strip above the same sentence.
data: the risk board: rows ranked by band with reasons, stage, owed items and drafts — computed server-side by tools/lib/risk.mjs from coach-teams.json, sessions and chat digests
the period: data/program.json meta.milestones through src/lib/period.ts — the due date counts as open on the day itself, weeks round down
setup facts: extension present, selected CLI usable (cli-probe), Microsoft sign-in — only what stops work
openQuestions: RESOLVED 2026-08-21: migrated onto OverviewPageTemplate. The block grew the `board` slot for exactly this anatomy (a ranked board as the centre of gravity, not a widget grid) — the live case completing the template rather than bending to it. header→title/actions, notices→SetupNeeded+PastMeetings, band→PeriodStrip, board→RiskBoard.

behaviours.given: a team whose card carries facts, chats read and items delivered
behaviours.then: none of that evidence adds points — a busy team scores no differently than a quiet one with the same risks
behaviours.why: Evidence sits beside the verdict; letting it move the score would reward noise.

behaviours.given: the board with a team card
behaviours.when: a keyboard or the usage tracker reaches for the card's door
behaviours.then: the door is a real control (a button), reachable and countable — never a clickable div
behaviours.why: The cockpit's main action once measured as never used because a div is invisible to both a keyboard and the tracker.
